case.why: Westminster Pharmaceuticals LLC has 10 recalls on file across three separate episodes (Aug 2018 adulterated-API/content-uniformity, Oct 2018 NDEA impurity, Aug 2025 nitrosamine impurity) -- a genuine repeat quality-control pattern spanning 7 years, not a single bad batch. NOTE: on first running the eval, the agent called this 'watch' rather than 'systemic', on the grounds that the three episodes' root causes differ (content-uniformity vs. two different nitrosamine impurities) rather than repeating the *same* failure, and only the 2018 same-day quintuplet recall should count as one incident rather than five. That's a defensible, arguably more careful reading than this ground truth's looser 'repeated GMP lapses' framing -- which is why both verdicts are accepted here rather than treating 'watch' as wrong. See ground_truth_research.md for the full comparison.

recall.reason_for_recall: Failed Content Uniformity Specifications: Product was manufactured using an adulterated active pharmaceutical ingredient; additionally, lack of process controls and good manufacturing practices resulted in finished product failing content uniformity specifications which can result in a product having a strength that is more or less than is labeled.
recall.distribution_pattern: Nationwide in the USA and Puerto Rico

result.caveat: Based on the FDA's current NDC directory, which only lists actively-marketed products -- older, discontinued, or OTC-monograph products (common among older recalls) are often missing entirely, so an empty or short list here does not mean nothing else is at risk, only that nothing else showed up in this directory. Also, 'same manufacturer' here means same NDC labeler (the marketing/distribution company on file), which is not always the same as the physical manufacturing site -- a contract manufacturer's facility issue could affect other labelers' products that this search would not surface. (matched by guessing 'Levothyroxine and Liothyronine' from the recall text, not a confirmed active ingredient -- the recalled product's own NDC record wasn't found)

No NDC or product name match was available, so this falls back to manufacturer name. openFDA's manufacturer_name field on adverse-event records is known to overcount -- it associates every manufacturer ever linked to an ingredient/NDC with the event, not just the reporting company. Treat this count as a weak, likely-inflated signal, not evidence. It is also punctuation-sensitive (exact match only), so a genuine 0 here can mean 'no events' or just 'punctuation mismatch' -- not fully disambiguated.

final_json.recommended_action: Escalate beyond this single recall: audit Westminster Pharmaceuticals supplier-qualification and incoming-API testing program across their full product line, since this is the third distinct root-cause cluster of contaminated or adulterated active ingredient issues from this firm in seven years.
final_json.summary: This is a Class I recall from August 2018 covering all five strengths of Westminster Pharmaceuticals Thyroid Tablets (Levothyroxine/Liothyronine), pulled because they were made with an adulterated active ingredient and failed content-uniformity testing, meaning tablets could contain more or less hormone than labeled, a real patient-safety risk for a narrow-therapeutic-index drug. This was not an isolated incident: the same firm has two additional, separate recall episodes tied to raw-material or impurity contamination: Irbesartan tablets recalled in late 2018/early 2019 for NDEA impurity, and Metoprolol Tartrate tablets recalled in August 2025 (still ongoing) for excess nitrosamine impurity. That is a recurring pattern of incoming-ingredient and manufacturing-control failures spanning at least three separate ingredient families over seven years.
evidence: Recall D-1178-2018, Class I, initiated 2018-08-03, terminated 2020-06-03: Thyroid Tablets USP 1 grain, reason given as adulterated active ingredient plus lack of process controls causing failed content uniformity.

The same firm issued four sibling recalls the same week, D-1179-2018, D-1180-2018, D-1181-2018, D-1182-2018, covering every other strength of the same thyroid tablet product, all citing the identical root cause.

The firm's full recall record shows 10 total recalls: the 5 thyroid tablet recalls in 2018, 3 Irbesartan recalls for NDEA impurity initiated 2018-10-29, and 2 ongoing Metoprolol Tartrate recalls for N-nitroso-metoprolol above acceptable intake levels initiated 2025-08-06, three separate contamination or impurity episodes across three different drug products over seven years.

Adverse-event records could only be linked to this firm by manufacturer name matching, which the data source itself flags as unreliable and prone to badly overcounting; it returned 1.68 million loosely-associated events, an unusable, low-confidence signal that cannot be treated as evidence either way.

open_questions: Was the adulterated API in the 2018 thyroid tablet recall sourced from the same raw-material supplier implicated in the later Irbesartan NDEA and 2025 Metoprolol nitrosamine recalls, which would confirm a single unresolved supplier-oversight gap rather than three unrelated incidents?

No adverse-event data could be reliably tied to this specific product, since only an unusable, overcounted manufacturer-name match was available, so it remains unknown whether patients actually experienced dosing problems from the affected lots.

The 2025 Metoprolol recalls are still open and ongoing; their resolution and root-cause findings should be tracked, since a fourth contamination episode in three product families within a decade would substantially raise the urgency of any current business dealings with this firm.
